By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and law s of the  
United States of Am erica, and to eliminate Executive Orders that are no  
longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and  
any amendments thereto, are revoked:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10872 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 2379, Federal Register of March 22, 1960, signed March 18, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employes, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 17, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Pan American World Airways, Inc., or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 128 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 2, 1960; the board report states that the board was granted an extension of time to report to June 2, 1960. Thirty days after June 2, 1960 is July 2, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 2, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 2, 1960.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10872
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE-  
TWEEN T H E  P A N  AMERICAN 
WORLD AIRWAYS, INC., A N D  
CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pan American World Airways, Inc.,  
a carrier, and certain of its employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
way and Steamship Clerks, Freight Han­
dlers, Express and Station Employes, a  
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW,. THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or by its employees, in the  
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 3567, the issue of April 26, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10875, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 22, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 22, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 130 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 8, 1960; the report's table of contents lists a letter of extension of the time limit. Thirty days after June 8, 1960 is July 8, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 8, 1960. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10888 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 9361, Federal Register of September 30, 1960, signed September 28, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between certain carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers' Conference Committee (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by labor organizations that are members of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, AFL-CIO (listed in attached List B); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by October 28, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 133 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated December 10, 1960; the report states that the time for filing it was extended to December 10, 1960 by the President on the consent of the parties. Thirty days after December 10, 1960 is January 9, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on December 10, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on January 9, 1961.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10888
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN CERTAIN CARRIERS REP­
RESENTED BY THE NEW YORK  
HARBOR CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE  
COMMITTEE A N D  CERTAIN OF  
THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
certain carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, designated in List A attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof, 
and certain of their employees repre­
sented by labor organizations, members 
of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, 
AFL-CIO, designated in List B attached 
hereto and hereby made a part hereof; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended 
(45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of 
railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by carriers represented by the New 
York Harbor Carriers’  Conference Com­
mittee, or by their employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10919 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". This order (26 FR 1463, Federal Register of February 21, 1961, signed February 17, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Flight Engineers' International Association, PAA Chapter, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by March 19, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Pan American World Airways, Inc., or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 135 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 20, 1961. Thirty days after June 20, 1961 is July 20, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 20, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 20, 1961. Executive Order 10926 (signed March 18, 1961; 26 FR 2331, Federal Register of March 21, 1961) extends until June 20, 1961 the time within which the board created by this order is to report its findings to the President; it does not revoke or supersede this order. It is recorded as a later event on this clause and is not an end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10923 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes". This order (26 FR 1699, Federal Register of February 28, 1961, signed February 24, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, a labor organization (two disputes, identified as National Mediation Board Cases A-6176 and A-6343); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by March 26, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 136 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 24, 1961; the report states that the President extended the time limit twice, the last extension being to May 24, 1961, while Executive Order 10933 authorizes a report on any day prior to May 24, 1961, a difference of one day that is disclosed. Thirty days after May 24, 1961 is June 23, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 24, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 23, 1961. Executive Order 10933 (signed April 12, 1961; 26 FR 3185, Federal Register of April 14, 1961) authorizes the board created by this order to make its report on any day prior to May 24, 1961 and provides that the thirty-day period following the report is deemed included in the extension; it does not revoke or supersede this order. It is recorded as a later event on this clause and is not an end.

Executive Order 10923
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE NORTHWEST AIR­
LINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS  
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS two disputes exist between  
the Northwest Airlines, Inc., a carrier,  
and certain of its employees represented  
by the International Association of M a­
chinists, a labor organization, identified  
as National Mediation Board Cases  
A-6176 and A-6343; and  
W HEREAS these disputes have not  
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to  
deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate these disputes. No mem­
ber of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to these dis­
putes within thirty days from the date of  
this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date end for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Northwest Airlines, Inc., or  
by its employees, in the conditions out of  
which these disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10965 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". This order (26 FR 9451, Federal Register of October 7, 1961, signed October 5, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 4, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Trans World Airlines, Inc. or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 140 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated November 3, 1961; the board's letter of transmittal is dated November 1, 1961 and the printed report cover is dated November 3, 1961, so the report date is disclosed as November 1-3, 1961. Thirty days after November 3, 1961 is December 3, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on November 3, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on December 3, 1961.

Executive Order 10965
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE TRANS WORLD AIR­
LINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS  
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Trans World Airlines, Inc., a carrier, 
and certain of its employees represented 
by the Transport Workers Union of 
America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially' to interrupt 
interstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive a section of the country of 
essential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by Section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate this dispute. No member 
of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization 
of airline employees or any carrier.
9451

=== PDF page 4 of 80 ===
9452 THE PRESIDENT
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the dispute 
within thirty days from the date of this 
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Trans World Airlines, Inc. 
or by its employees, in the condition out 
of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11054 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry". This order (27 FR 9695, Federal Register of October 2, 1962, signed October 1, 1962) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships serving Atlantic and Gulf Coast ports from Searsport, Maine, to Brownsville, Texas, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO, disputes that had resulted in a strike; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 by a Thursday in October 1962 (the day of the month is garbled in the text layer); and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so none is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation. The text layer of this order is badly garbled in places, so this description is a paraphrase of the legible words and no part of it is quoted.

The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers unrelated Federal Register rules on neighbouring pages, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (a Thursday in October 1962) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The deadline is not an end and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence) depends on this order and on the disputes it addressed; the Board's statutory powers come from the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the disputes were one-time disputes.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried by correction: the whole operative text (the recitals of the maritime disputes and strike, the creation and membership of the Board of Inquiry, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the disputes were one-time disputes. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11101 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 3305, Federal Register of April 5, 1963, signed April 3, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, and the Switchmen's Union of North America, labor organizations; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 154 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 13, 1963. Thirty days after May 13, 1963 is June 12, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 13, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 12, 1963.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 3305, the issue of April 5, 1963) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11101, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 3, 1963. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11115 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 6905, Federal Register of July 6, 1963, signed July 4, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Pullman Company, The Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by August 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those four carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 155 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated November 2, 1963; the board report states that the parties agreed to extensions of time to September 19, October 19 and finally to November 2, 1963 with the approval of the President. Thirty days after November 2, 1963 is December 2, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on November 2, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on December 2, 1963.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11115
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE PULLMAN COMPANY, THE CHICAGO, ROCK ISLAND &
PACIFIC RAILROAD COMPANY, THE NEW YORK CENTRAL SYSTEM,
AND THE SOO LINE RAILROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF THEIR
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between The Pullman Company, The  
Chicago, Rock Island &  Pacific Railroad Company, the New York  
Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain  
of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car  
Porters, a labor organization;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees  
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Pullman Company, the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad  
Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad  
Company, or by its employees, in the conditions out of which this  
dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11131 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes". This order (28 FR 13485, Federal Register of December 13, 1963, signed December 11, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Braniff Airways, Inc., Continental Airlines, Inc., Eastern Air Lines, Inc., National Airlines, Inc., Northwest Airlines, Inc., and Trans World Airlines, Inc., air carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by January 10, 1964); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those six air carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by January 10, 1964) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 13485, the issue of December 13, 1963) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11131, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated December 11, 1963. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by January 10, 1964), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by January 10, 1964) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11181 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime indusiry". This order (29 FR 13557, Federal Register of October 2, 1964, signed September 30, 1964) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Herbert Schmertz as chairman, James J. Healy and Theodore W. Kheel) to inquire into the issues in labor disputes between maritime-industry employers (steamship companies, operators or agents of ships, contracting stevedores, contracting marine carpenters, lighterage operators and other employers in related pier activities) and certain of their employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before Thursday, October 1, 1964; and provided that upon the submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the order's own continuing-existence sentence means its text does not end the Board when the report is submitted. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (29 FR 13557, the issue of October 2, 1964) is Executive Order 11181, dated September 30, 1964; the order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 for labor disputes affecting the maritime industry, and carries the signature date September 30, 1964. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (on or before Thursday, October 1, 1964) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report to perform other functions required under the Act; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers and duties by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence after the report) depends on this order and on the dispute it addressed; the powers and procedures are those of the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute that does not depend on this order.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself, not of this order, and the dispute was a one-time dispute.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text (the recitals of the maritime disputes and threatened strike, the creation and membership of the Board of Inquiry, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, so every command in the clause ends on the same date."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself, not of this order, and the dispute was a one-time dispute. No held claim-grade source shows any command of this order continuing when it was revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11321 with the subject "Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the military aircraft engine industry". This order (31 FR 16301, Federal Register of December 21, 1966, signed December 19, 1966) created, under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), a Board of Inquiry of three named members (Laurence E. Seibel as chairman, Frank J. Dugan and Garth L. Mangum) to inquire into the issues in the labor dispute between the Union Carbide Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO, and Local Union No. 2958 thereof, involving the Stellite Division plant at Kokomo, Indiana, a dispute that had resulted in a strike affecting the military aircraft engine industry; gave the Board the powers and duties set forth in Title II of the Act; directed it to report to the President in accordance with section 206 on or before December 20, 1966; and provided that upon submission of its report the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the Act. The report date is a deadline, not an end, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), and the continuing-existence sentence means the order's own text does not end the Board at the report. No report of this Board is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent as to its reporting deadline, and the order stayed on the books until this express revocation.

CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE
AFFECTING THE MILITARY AIRCRAFT ENGINE INDUSTRY OF THE
UNITED STATES
W HEREAS, there exists a labor dispute between the Union Carbide  
Corporation, a New York Corporation, and certain of its employees  
represented by the United Steelworkers of America, AFL-CIO, and  
Local Union No. 2958 thereof, involving the Stellite Division plant of  
Union Carbide Corporation located at Kokomo, Indiana; and
W HEREAS, such dispute has resulted in a strike which will, in  
my opinion, if permitted to continue, affect a substantial part of the  
military aircraft engine industry, which industry isengaged in trade,  
commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the  
several States or with foreign nations, or engaged in the production of  
goods for commerce, and which strike, if permitted to continue, will  
imperil the national safety:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat.  
155; 29 U.S.C. 176), I hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of  
Mr. Laurence E. Seibel, Chairman, Mr. Frank J. Dugan and Mr.  
Garth L. Mangum, whom I appoint to inquire into the issues involved  
in this dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II  
of such Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance  
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before December  
20,1966.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence  
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (31 FR 16301, the issue of December 21, 1966) is Executive Order 11321, dated December 19, 1966; it is headed with the title Creating a Board of Inquiry to Report on a Labor Dispute Affecting the Military Aircraft Engine Industry of the United States, names the Union Carbide Corporation dispute, and is dated December 19, 1966. The dossier's clause inventory for this order covers neighbouring Federal Register documents, not this order, so I replaced it with the order's own operative text. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier. 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states a report deadline (on or before December 20, 1966) and a sentence that the Board shall continue in existence after its report; it states no date on which the Board or the order ends. The deadline is not an end and the continuing-existence sentence is the opposite of an own-terms end at the report. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553, and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 shows no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create and appoint the Board, state its powers by reference to Title II of the Act, set the report deadline, continue the Board in existence) depends on this order and on the one dispute it addressed; the Board's statutory powers come from the Labor-Management Relations Act, a separate statute.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. The Board's statutory functions under the Labor-Management Relations Act are those of the Act itself and the dispute was a one-time dispute.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried by correction: the whole operative text (the recitals of the dispute and strike, the creation and membership of the Board, its powers and duties, the report deadline and the continuing-existence sentence). The dossier's sixteen clauses are neighbouring documents on the same pages and are not clauses of this order. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11324 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 1075, Federal Register of January 31, 1967, signed January 28, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship Builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers & Helpers, Sheet Metal Workers' International Association, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Brotherhood Railway Carmen of America, and International Brotherhood of Firemen and Oilers, functioning through the Railway Employes' Department, AFL-CIO (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 27, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 27, 1967) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace 
Workers; International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, Iron Ship­
builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers &  Helpers; Sheet Metal Workers’  
International Association; International Brotherhood of Electrical 
Workers; Brotherhood Railway Carmen of America; International 
Brotherhood of Firemen and Oilers functioning through the Railway 
Employes’  Department, AFL-CIO, labor organizations; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board ox three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (32 FR 1075, the issue of January 31, 1967) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11324, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 28, 1967. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 27, 1967), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 27, 1967) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11343 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 6085, Federal Register of April 18, 1967, signed April 12, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Long Island Rail Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, labor organizations (three disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 12, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by The Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 170 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 12, 1967. Thirty days after May 12, 1967 is June 11, 1967. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 12, 1967, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 11, 1967.

WHEREAS, three disputes exist between The Long Island Rail

Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of  
Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and  
Aerospace Workers, labor organizations;  and

WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to such a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:

Section 10 of the Railway Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby

these disputes within 30 days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out  
< ? f which these disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11443 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (34 FR 541, Federal Register of January 15, 1969, signed January 13, 1969) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor organization (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 12, 1969); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by February 12, 1969) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor 
organization; and
WHEREAS these disputes haye not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the Board shall be pecuniar­
ily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (34 FR 541, the issue of January 15, 1969) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11443, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 13, 1969. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11622 with the subject "Amending an order creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime". This order (36 FR 19491, Federal Register of October 7, 1971, signed October 5, 1971) lead sentence: by virtue of the authority vested in the President by section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 155; 29 U.S.C. 176), Executive Order 11621 of October 4, 1971 is amended as set out in items (1) and (2).

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11622 with the subject "Amending an order creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime". operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11622 with the subject "Amending an order creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime". This order (36 FR 19491, Federal Register of October 7, 1971, signed October 5, 1971) item (2) amends the third paragraph of Executive Order 11621 by deleting the name Morris L. Myers.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11663 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (37 FR 6647, Federal Register of April 1, 1972, signed March 31, 1972) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached lists) and certain of their employees represented by the Sheet Metal Workers' International Association, a labor organization (disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 30, 1972); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated April 30, 1972. Thirty days after April 30, 1972 is May 30, 1972. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on April 30, 1972, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on May 30, 1972.
