=== PDF page 7 of 88 ===
Presidential Documents
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
and Certain of Their Employees
WHEREAS, disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees represented by 
the Sheet Metal Workers’  International Association, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS, these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS, these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive sections of the country of essential transporta­
tion service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board, of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its finding to the President with respect to 
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.
Title 3—The President
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11663

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (37 FR 6647, the issue of April 1, 1972) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11663, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated March 31, 1972. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 30, 1972), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated April 30, 1972. Thirty days after April 30, 1972 is May 30, 1972. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on April 30, 1972, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on May 30, 1972. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11694 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (38 FR 729, Federal Register of January 4, 1973, signed January 2, 1973) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by February 1, 1973); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of the board created by this order (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated February 1, 1973. Thirty days after February 1, 1973 is March 3, 1973. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on February 1, 1973, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on March 3, 1973.

Presidential Docum ents
Creating an Emergency Board to Investigate a Dispute Between the
Port Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation and Certain of Its
Employees
W H EREAS, a dispute exists between the Port Authority Trans-Hudson 
Corporation and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood 
Railway Carmen of the United States and Canada, a labor organization; 
and
W H EREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H EREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a de­
gree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation 
service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from 
this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the 
President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Port 
Authority Trans-Hudson Corporation, or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which the dispute arose.
Title 3—The President

Identity: the held Federal Register text (38 FR 729, the issue of January 4, 1973) is the order itself: its number, Executive Order 11694, is printed in a displaced heading after the text, and it creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated January 2, 1973. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11745 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (38 FR 30429, Federal Register of November 5, 1973, signed November 1, 1973) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by December 1, 1973); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by December 1, 1973) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

THE PRESIDENT 30429
E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  11745
Creating an Em ergency Board T o  Investigate a  Dispute Between the 
L ong Island R ail R oad and Certain o f Its Employees
W HEREAS, a dispute exists between the Long Island Rail Road and 
certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, A F L -C IO , a labor organization; and
W HEREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transpor­
tation service:
N O W , TH E R EF O R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out of 
which the dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (38 FR 30429, the issue of November 5, 1973) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11745, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated November 1, 1973. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by December 1, 1973), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11797 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (39 FR 27893, Federal Register of August 2, 1974, signed July 31, 1974) authorizes, under section 901(b) of the Agricultural Act of 1970 (84 Stat. 1383), as amended by section 601 of the Rural Development Act of 1972 (86 Stat. 674; Public Law 92-419), and section 301 of title 3 of the United States Code, the Secretary of Agriculture to exercise the authority vested in the President by section 901(b) in all matters relating to reporting criteria and the preparation and submission of annual reports to the Congress concerning the location of new Federal facilities in rural areas, without approval, ratification or other action by the President; and directs departments and agencies to cooperate with the Secretary in preparing the annual reports required by section 901(b). It is a continuing delegation with no stated end date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11805 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (39 FR 34261, Federal Register of September 24, 1974, signed September 20, 1974) orders that any return defined in section 301.6103(a)-1 of the Treasury Regulations on Procedure and Administration (26 CFR Part 301), as amended from time to time, made in respect of any tax described in section 301.6103(a)-1(a)(2), shall be delivered to or open to inspection by the President only upon a written request signed by the President personally; prescribes the contents of the request (the name and address of the taxpayer, the kind of return and the taxable period), addressed to the Secretary of the Treasury or his delegate; allows the President to designate by name employees of the White House Office holding a Presidential commission with an annual rate of basic pay at or above that prescribed by 5 U.S.C. 5316; bars disclosure by such an employee except to the President without the President's written direction; and subjects all persons obtaining access to the return to 26 U.S.C. 6103, as amended. It states no end date.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue o f the authority vested in m e as President of the United 
States, and in the interest o f protecting the right o f taxpayers to privacy 
and confidentiality regarding their tax affairs consistent with proper 
internal management o f the Government, and in the further interest o f 
maintaining the integrity o f the self-assessment system o f Federal taxation, 
it is hereby ordered that any return, as defined in Section 301.6103 ( a ) - l  
o f the Treasury Regulations on Procedure and Administration (26 C F R  
Part 301) as amended from  time to time, made by a taxpayer in respect 
o f any tax described in Section 301.6103(a)— 1(a)(2)  o f such regula­
tions shall be delivered to or open to inspection by the President only 
upon written request signed by the President personally.
Any such request for delivery or inspection shall be addressed to the 
Secretary o f the Treasury or his. delegate and shall state: ( i) the name 
and address o f the taxpayer whose return is to be inspected, (ii)  the kind 
o f return or returns which are to be inspected, and (iii)  the taxable period 
or periods covered by such return or returns.
In any such request for delivery or inspection, the President may 
designate by name an employee or employees o f the W hite House O ffice 
w ho are authorized on behalf o f the President to receive any such return 
or make such inspection, provided that the President will not so designate 
an employee unless such employee is the holder o f a Presidential com ­
mission whose annual rate o f basic pay equals or exceeds the annual rate 
o f basic pay prescribed by 5 U .S.C . 5316. N o disclosure o f such return, 
or any data contained therein or derived therefrom shall be made by such 
employee except to the President, without the written direction o f the 
President.
A ll persons obtaining access to such return, or any data contained 
therein or derived therefrom shall in all respects be subject to the pro­

By virtue o f the authority vested in m e as President of the United 
States, and in the interest o f protecting the right o f taxpayers to privacy 
and confidentiality regarding their tax affairs consistent with proper 
internal management o f the Government, and in the further interest o f 
maintaining the integrity o f the self-assessment system o f Federal taxation, 
it is hereby ordered that any return, as defined in Section 301.6103 ( a ) - l  
o f the Treasury Regulations on Procedure and Administration (26 C F R  
Part 301) as amended from  time to time, made by a taxpayer in respect 
o f any tax described in Section 301.6103(a)— 1(a)(2)  o f such regula­
tions shall be delivered to or open to inspection by the President only 
upon written request signed by the President personally.
Any such request for delivery or inspection shall be addressed to the 
Secretary o f the Treasury or his. delegate and shall state: ( i) the name 
and address o f the taxpayer whose return is to be inspected, (ii)  the kind 
o f return or returns which are to be inspected, and (iii)  the taxable period 
or periods covered by such return or returns.
In any such request for delivery or inspection, the President may 
designate by name an employee or employees o f the W hite House O ffice 
w ho are authorized on behalf o f the President to receive any such return 
or make such inspection, provided that the President will not so designate 
an employee unless such employee is the holder o f a Presidential com ­
mission whose annual rate o f basic pay equals or exceeds the annual rate 
o f basic pay prescribed by 5 U .S.C . 5316. N o disclosure o f such return, 
or any data contained therein or derived therefrom shall be made by such 
employee except to the President, without the written direction o f the 
President.
A ll persons obtaining access to such return, or any data contained 
therein or derived therefrom shall in all respects be subject to the pro­
visions o f 26 U .S.C . 6103, as amended.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11852 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (40 FR 17239, Federal Register of April 18, 1975, signed April 16, 1975) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached lists) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 11852
Creating an Emergency Board T o  Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
and Certain o f Their Employees
A  dispute exists between the carriers represented by the National 
Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain o f its employees represented by the Brother­
hood o f Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, 
Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; '
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions 
o f the Railway Labor A ct, as am ended; and
This dispute, in the judgm ent o f the National M ediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce to a degree such 
as to deprive a section o f the country o f essential transportation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in m e by 
Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended (45 U .S.C . 1 6 0 ), 
I hereby create a board o f three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o m em ber o f the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization o f railroad employees or 
any carrier.
T he board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within 30 days from  the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended, 
from  this date and for 30 days after the board has made its report to 
the President, n o change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (40 FR 17239, the issue of April 18, 1975) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11852, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 16, 1975. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
